messages.author: 17d9c7a6e1a581b8
messages.subject: PyStan alpha
parts:
PyStan alpha available at:

https://github.com/ariddell/pystan

It works out of the box if you're on 64-bit linux.

Right now libstan.a and libstanc.a are included in the package because I haven't
yet figured out how to get Python to compile them during install. If you have
Python 3.3 on a 64-bit linux you should be able to run the important parts right
away. See

https://github.com/ariddell/pystan/blob/master/doc/getting_started.rst

Best,

Allen

messages.author: 17d9c7a6e1a581b8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] PyStan alpha
parts:
PyStan might work on Windows, Mac and other Linuxes now.

Regardless of the platform, Cython and Numpy need to be installed along with
a C++ compiler. If you can install NumPy from source on your system you should
be able to build Stan/PyStan. Feedback would be appreciated.

If you folks would prefer a different implementation I'd be happy to change the
package name from PyStan to something else. I don't want to step on anyone's
toes.

Best,

Allen

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] PyStan alpha

Hey Allen,

I'm looking over it now and one quick comment: would it be possible to expose the choice of compiler?  Or maybe it already is, in which case how can I change compilers?  Being able to use clang instead of gcc can make building Stan (and Stan models!) *much* faster.

Anyway, so far it looks great and I'm really excited to be able to start using it more!

Cheers,
Marcus
